authors: Jing Fan; Miao He; Chuan-Jiang Wang; Mu Zhang

abstract: This study investigated the role of IL-27 and liver macrophages in liver injury following severe infection. Gadolinium chloride inhibited IL-27 production and M1 macrophage polarization, reducing liver injury in a mouse model.

title: Interleukins-27 Aggravates Liver Injury by Impairing the Antimicrobial Response of Macrophages via the Promotion of Mitochondrial Dysfunction in the Context of Sepsis
authors: Yuehua You; Yuyan Li; Lin Ye; Fang Xu; Jing Fan
abstract: IL-27 exacerbates liver injury in sepsis by impairing macrophage antimicrobial responses. This occurs through IL-27-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, which reduces bacterial clearance.

title: IL-27 neutralization enhances macrophage polarization and improves immune checkpoint efficacy
authors: Quentin Glaziou, Laetitia Basset, Sènan d’Almeida, Pascale Pignon, Nabila Jabrane-Ferrat, Christophe...
id: Matched: IL-27 neutralization during macrophage differentiation reduces immunos
abstract: IL-27 neutralization was studied for its effects on tumor-associated macrophages and the tumor immune microenvironment. Blocking IL-27 repolarized macrophages, enhancing T cell responses and immune checkpoint therapy efficacy.

title: Macrophage Cytokines: Involvement in Immunity and Infectious Diseases
authors: Guillermo Arango Duque; Albert Descoteaux
abstract: This review examines macrophage-secreted cytokines and their release mechanisms. These cytokines are crucial for immunity and infectious disease, with dysregulation contributing to various pathologies.

title: IL-27 regulation of innate immunity and control of microbial growth
authors: Jessica M Povroznik; Cory M Robinson
abstract: This paper examines how IL-27 regulates innate immune cells and their responses to pathogens. IL-27 signaling suppresses key innate immune functions, impacting inflammation and microbial control.

title: IL-27 Aggravates Sepsis-Induced ARDS by Driving Macrophage Ferroptosis Through Activation of NCOA4-Mediated Ferritinophagy
authors: Minkang Guo; Meng Xiong; Jindian Shi; Qiaozhi Peng; Shihui Lin; Fang Xu
id: Matched: Inhibiting Ferritinophagy Effectively Alleviates the Inflammatory Resp
abstract: IL-27 worsens sepsis-induced ARDS by promoting macrophage ferroptosis. It achieves this by activating NCOA4, which drives ferritinophagy and M1 polarization. A novel NCOA4 degrader, CV3, reverses these effects, offering a potential therapeutic strategy.

title: STAT-3 is necessary for IL-27-mediated macrophage suppression but does not represent a therapeutic target for E. coli-induced neonatal sepsis
authors: Madhavi Annamanedi; Jessica M. Povroznik; Cory M. Robinson
abstract: STAT-3 is necessary for IL-27's suppression of bacterial clearance and inflammation in neonatal macrophages. However, targeting STAT-3 in macrophages does not improve outcomes in E. coli-induced neonatal sepsis.

title: IL-27 amplifies cytokine responses to Gram-negative bacterial products and Salmonella typhimurium infection
authors: C. Petes; N. Odoardi; S. M. Plater; N. L. Martin; K. Gee
id: Matched: Co-stimulation of LPS and IL-27 upregulates proinflammatory cytokine e
abstract: This study investigated IL-27's effect on human monocyte and macrophage responses to bacterial products and infection. IL-27 amplified pro-inflammatory cytokine production in response to LPS and *Salmonella typhimurium* infection.

title: Synergistic Effects of Toll-Like Receptor 1/2 and Toll-Like Receptor 3 Signaling Triggering Interleukin 27 Gene Expression in Chikungunya Virus-Infected Macrophages
authors: Juan Felipe Valdés-López; Geysson J. Fernandez; Silvio Urcuqui-Inchima
id: Matched: 3.12 TLR4 Activation in Human and Murine Macrophages Induces IL27 Expr
abstract: This study investigated how Toll-like receptor signaling affects IL-27 gene expression in macrophages infected with Chikungunya virus. Synergistic activation of TLR1/2 and TLR3 pathways is required for functional IL-27 production, which then drives pro-inflammatory and antiviral responses independently of interferon signaling.

title: IL-23 and IL-27 Levels in Macrophages Collected from Peripheral Blood of Patients with Healing Vs Non-Healing Form of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
authors: S Tolouei; K Ghaedi; A Khamesipour; M Akbari; M Baghaei; SJ Hasheminia; M Narimani; SH Hejazi
abstract: This study compared IL-23 and IL-27 levels in macrophages from patients with healing versus non-healing cutaneous leishmaniasis. Macrophages from healing lesions produced significantly higher levels of both cytokines.

title: Interleukin-27 and Its Diverse Effects on Bacterial Infections
authors: Yugo Morita; Elysia A. Masters; Edward M. Schwarz; Gowrishankar Muthukrishnan
id: Matched: Overview of IL-27 Components, Receptors, Signaling Pathways
abstract: This review examines interleukin-27's diverse roles in bacterial infections. IL-27 exhibits both pro- and anti-inflammatory effects, potentially offering therapeutic regulation for infection outcomes.

abstract: This study investigated the association of IL-27 genetic polymorphisms with sepsis. The -964A>G polymorphism enhances IL-27 expression and inflammatory responses, increasing sepsis severity and mortality.

abstract: This review summarizes IL-27's role in inflammatory autoimmune diseases. IL-27's dual pro- and anti-inflammatory functions suggest it's a promising therapeutic target.

title: Elevated Levels of Interleukin-27 in Early Life Compromise Protective Immunity in a Mouse Model of Gram-Negative Neonatal Sepsis
authors: Brittany G. Seman; Jordan K. Vance; Travis W. Rawson; Michelle R. Witt; Annalisa B. Huckaby; Jessica...
abstract: Elevated IL-27 levels were observed in neonatal mice and human cord blood macrophages, and these levels increased during Gram-negative sepsis. This suggests IL-27 may compromise protective immunity in neonates, increasing sepsis severity.

title: Interleukin 27 is increased in carotid atherosclerosis and promotes NLRP3 inflammasome activation

abstract: This study investigated IL-27 in carotid atherosclerosis patients and its effects on the NLRP3 inflammasome. IL-27 was elevated in patients and promoted inflammasome activation in monocytes, suggesting a role in disease development.

title: IL-27-Ucp2-FoxO3 axis mediating the polarization of alternatively activated macrophages and ameliorating inflammatory pain
authors: Yi Ma; Shuyuan Gan; Yueying Zheng; Xianhui Kang; Shengmei Zhu
abstract: IL-27 promotes anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization by reprogramming their metabolism via Ucp2 and activating FoxO3. This IL-27-Ucp2-FoxO3 axis effectively alleviates inflammatory pain in mice.

title: Regulation of IL-27 p28 gene expression in macrophages through MyD88- and interferon-γ–mediated pathways
authors: Jianguo Liu; Xiuqin Guan; Xiaojing Ma
abstract: This study investigated how inflammatory signals regulate the mouse IL-27 p28 gene in macrophages. LPS and IFN-γ induce p28 production through MyD88-dependent pathways, with additional dependencies on c-Rel and IRF1 respectively.

title: Integrated Functional and scRNA-Seq Analyses Reveal Convergence of M-CSF– and GM-CSF–Derived Macrophages Following IL-27 Polarization
authors: Tomozumi Imamichi; Jun Yang; Qian Chen; Udeshika Kariyawasam; Mayra Marquez; Jeanette Higgins; Jorda...
abstract: IL-27 reprograms macrophages derived from different precursors into a similar state. This convergent polarization suggests IL-27 plays a key role in regulating macrophage plasticity and function.

abstract: IL-27-polarized macrophages were studied for their HIV resistance and gene expression. These macrophages resist HIV through distinct antiviral gene expression patterns in individual cells, suggesting a novel subtype.

authors: Caroline Andrews; Mairi H. McLean; Julie A. Hixon; Sergio M. Pontejo; Tregei Starr; Courtney Malo; M...
abstract: Murine macrophages were studied for their response to IL-27. IL-27 induces an IFN-like signature in macrophages, which then produce factors that affect colonic epithelium.

authors: Ralf Watzlawick; Elisabeth E. Kenngott; Francesca Diane M. Liu; Jan M. Schwab; Alf Hamann
abstract: IL-27 was studied for its anti-inflammatory effects in zymosan-induced peritonitis. It was found to reduce neutrophil recruitment by impairing bone marrow mobilization and lowering chemokine levels.
